questions.q: Explain the heating effect of electric current and its uses.
answer: When an electric current flows through a wire, the wire becomes hot. This is called the heating effect of current.

answer.text: The greater the resistance of the wire, the more heat is produced for a given current. Appliances that need to produce heat use a special high-resistance wire, often made of nichrome.
The heating effect is used in electric heaters, irons, geysers and toasters. In an electric bulb, current heats a thin tungsten filament until it glows and gives light.
The same effect makes the electric fuse a safety device: a thin wire in the fuse melts and breaks the circuit if too much current flows, preventing wires from overheating and causing fire.

questions.q: What is the magnetic effect of current, and how does an electromagnet work?
answer: A wire carrying an electric current behaves like a magnet; this is called the magnetic effect of current, first shown by Oersted, who saw a compass needle deflect near a current-carrying wire.

answer.text: An electromagnet is made by winding a coil of insulated wire around a piece of iron, called the core. When current flows through the coil, the iron becomes a strong magnet, and when the current is switched off, it loses its magnetism.
Because it can be switched on and off and made very strong, the electromagnet is used in cranes to lift iron, and in electric bells, motors and loudspeakers.

answer: Thus electricity and magnetism are closely linked.
